title: Auto-detect R package in well-known GitHub subdirectories
description:
## Summary

Closes #459.

GitHub remotes now auto-detect an R package in a well-known subdirectory (`pkg-r/`, `r/`, or `R/`) when no `subdir` is given and there is no `DESCRIPTION` at the repository root. This lets multi-language repositories (e.g. a Python package, a JS frontend, and an R package each in their own subdirectory) be installed with `pak::pkg_install("owner/repo")` without the caller knowing where the R package lives.

### Behavior

- **Probing only when no `subdir` is supplied.** If an explicit `subdir` is given, only that single path is queried — unchanged behavior, including the existing "no package" error for that directory.
- **Priority order (first match wins): repo root → `pkg-r/` → `r/` → `R/`.** The root always takes precedence, so repos with a root `DESCRIPTION` resolve exactly as before (and produce no `RemoteSubdir`).
- **Silent**: the detected subdir is threaded into the resolution's `RemoteSubdir` metadata; no message is emitted.
- Applies to all three GitHub resolution variants: plain ref, pull request (`#NN`), and release (`@*release`).

### Mechanism

A single GraphQL query probes all candidate `DESCRIPTION` paths in one round-trip using GraphQL aliases. Because GitHub's GraphQL rate limit is computed from connections (paginated `first`/`last` fields), not from single-node `object`/`file` lookups, the aliased query costs the **same 1 point and one round-trip** as today — including for normal root-`DESCRIPTION` repos.

### Implementation notes

- New internal helpers in `R/type-github.R` (candidate list, alias-fragment builders, and a shared response picker) keep the three variants DRY.
- `check_github_response_*` were slimmed: the "is this a package?" / binary checks now live in the shared picker, while query/ref/release errors stay in the per-variant checkers. All original errors are preserved (`no_package`, `baddesc`, `noref`, `no_release`, query errors).
- The fake GitHub GraphQL test server (`R/gh-app.R`) was made alias-aware so it answers both the new aliased queries and legacy single-field queries.

## Test Plan

- [x] New unit tests for the pure helpers (`tests/testthat/test-type-github-subdir.R`).
- [x] New integration tests through the fake server: auto-detect `pkg-r/` for ref/pull/release; `r/`-over-`R/` priority; root → no `RemoteSubdir`; no-package-anywhere → failure; explicit-subdir queried alone (no fallback).
- [x] `type-github` suite: 210 pass / 0 fail. `github-tools`: 31 pass / 0 fail (snapshot updated for the new internal `subdir` field). `type-git`: 243 pass / 0 fail.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

GitLab and generic `git::` remotes could adopt the same convention (cheaper there — the full file tree is already fetched). Gated on r-lib/pak#646.

title: Fix Windows release CI auth for GitHub dependency resolution
description:
The `windows-latest (release)` Actions job was failing during dependency setup because GitHub-backed dependencies could not authenticate while resolving `r-lib/pkgcache@feature/ppm-sso` and its `gaborcsardi/tstoml` remote. The workflow exposed `GITHUB_PAT`, but the CI code path in this repo reads `CI_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

- **Root cause**
  - `pkgdepends`' CI GitHub auth path prefers `CI_GITHUB_TOKEN`.
  - `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml` only exported `GITHUB_PAT`, so GitHub remote resolution in CI could fail with `Cannot query GitHub, are you offline?`.

- **Change**
  - Export `CI_GITHUB_TOKEN` in the R CMD check workflow, using the existing `secrets.CI_GITHUB_TOKEN`.
  - Keep `GITHUB_PAT` set to the same secret so both auth paths remain covered.

- **Workflow update**
  ```yaml
  env:
    CI_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CI_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.CI_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
  ```

- **Effect**
  - Aligns the workflow environment with the repository’s CI-specific GitHub auth behavior.
  - Unblocks GitHub remote resolution in the Windows release job without changing package code or dependency logic.

title: test: use a deterministic token for fake GitHub app tests
description:
## Summary

The new `test-coverage` workflow (`uncovr::test()`) runs the full testthat suite, unlike `R CMD check`, which only runs the `scan-deps` tests (`tests/testthat.R` filters to them). This surfaced 15 failures in `test-github-tools.R`: the fake GitHub app validates the `Authorization` header format via `re_gh_auth()`, but the tests relied on whatever ambient credential `type_github_get_headers()` found. On CI, `GITHUB_PAT` is set to `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`; with no git credential helper present, `gitcreds_get()` returns it, the fake app rejects it as malformed, and every snapshot fails with HTTP 401.

This makes the fake-app tests hermetic: `setup_fake_gh_app()` now pins all token sources (`CI_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_PAT_GITHUB_COM`, `GITHUB_PAT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to a deterministic, well-formed fake token, so requests never depend on ambient credentials. The `http error` test now calls `setup_fake_gh_app()` too (it set the API URL manually and missed the token vars). Tests that exercise bad-credential paths still set their own token values after `setup_fake_gh_app()`, so they are unaffected.

## Verification

Under a simulated CI runner (`CI=true`, no credential helper, a malformed ambient `GITHUB_PAT`): `test-github-tools.R` 31 passed (was 15 failing), `test-type-github.R` 177 passed, `test-type-url.R` 21 passed. All also pass in the normal local environment.

title: Make Posit Package Manager with binaries work if it doesn't need compilation
description:
This PR fixes an upstream issue reported in pak (https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/583#issuecomment-4010777798) where the requested package version is not always respected when using PPM.

As described in my latest comments in that issue (including an MWE), the problem occurs when using PPM binaries and the package does not require compilation. In that case, the platform is recorded as an empty string, which causes the binary to be rejected during platform matching.

This PR allows empty platform strings to match, which enables the correct binary to be downloaded.

title: Fix RHEL platform autodetection
description:
https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/610

Can likely be done more elegantly but should go into the right direction and move things forward.

RHEL is reported as follows

```r
pak::system_r_platform()
[1] "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-rhel-9.4"
>

pak::system_r_platform()
[1] "x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-rhel-9.4"
>

pak::system_r_platform()
[1] "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-rhel-8.10"
>

pak::system_r_platform()
[1] "x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-rhel-8.10"
>
```

Given that all RH-related sysdep mappings are referenced as `"redhat"`, rewriting the respective internal mappings made most sense to me.

This change results in the following

```r
sysreqs_install_plan("curl", config = list(sysreqs_platform = "x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-rhel-8.10"))

$os
[1] "linux"

$distribution
[1] "redhat"

$version
[1] "8"

$pre_install
character(0)

$install_scripts
character(0)

$post_install
character(0)
```

Given that `"redhat-8"` and `"redhat-9"` already work as desired when handed over manually, this change should align the platform parsing for the moment.

description:
Following on the comment in https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/issues/354#issuecomment-1981975911, this records a listing of paths in a git remote that failed to be parsed out of the packfile. Notably, this will allow for gracefully recovering from failing to clone submodules in cases where they are not required for the package to build, though it would apply in other instances as well.

Instead of failing immediately, this gives the opportunity to determine the severity of failing to parse the file tree out of the packfile and only throw an error if a file is necessary for the package to build.

This also implements a check for severity, disregarding files outside a remote subdir if one is provided, or files ignored in `.Rbuildignore`.

title: Updating GitLab url parsing; fix authed list_refs
description:
This PR is intended to fix #328 with a few other related fixes

* Updates parsing for GitLab remotes, which currently is forgetting a `/` between the host and "username". Unlike GitHub, GitLab allows arbitrary nesting of groups:
   | Service | Style |
   | --- | :-- |
   | GitHub | `username/repo` |
   | GitLab | `group/subgroup/subsubgroup/project` |
   
   This throws a wrench in the subdir parsing. To allow a subdir, I added a `/-/` separator:  
   `group/subgroup/project/-/sub/dir@ref`
   [`/-/` is a reserved name](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/reserved_names.html) used for other server paths, so there's no risk of conflict with project paths. 
* Calls to `/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` require authentication, which is currently ignored. I added this authentication to `async_git_list_refs_v2` and `async_git_send_message_v2`, necessary for solving package dependencies.

Let me know if I'm on the right track, or if you think this is better solved some other way.

title: Fix authentication in private git repos
description:
Fixes #319

Username and password may contain reserved URL characters (RFC 3986) `! * ' ( ) ; : @ & = + $ , / ? % # [ ]`, that must be escaped when embedded into the URL.

Most common case is username being user's email address.

title: WIP: Proof of concept implementation for local package caching
description:
This is a proof of concept implementation for #261

The basic idea is to leverage the fact that the metadata of installed packages is already cached. So we don't need to do much — just inject some metadata describing the contents of the local repository (in this initial draft it's the local path + the file checksums) and do nothing if they match the already installed package. Seems to work well enough in local tests, but I cannot exclude that I missed something crucial — the package logic is fairly complex and I barely scraped the surface of the iceberg in trying to understand it.  

The checksumming currently relies on `tools::md5sum()` and simply concatenates the hash for all files (just to show that it works), but we probably want to use `digest` here for proper sha256 (this would mean hard dependency on `digest` however). Otherwise we need to find a way to mix the md5 hashes somehow without introducing new package dependencies. Regarding performance: checksumming does introduce some overhead,  but making a package is still much much slower, so if you local packages do not change too often, amortized savings over time can be substantial.  

Please tell me what you think and I'll do my best to transition it to something more production ready.

title: Git fetch now robust to tree order
description:
As it stands, the pkgdepends code for unpacking git repo packfiles is sensitive to the order of the trees (#339). This doesn't seem to matter for git hosts that provide the trees in the order of deepest roots first but for those that don't the current unpacking code will provide incorrect results. This problem occurs for repos hosted on Azure DevOps, for example, where I've been experiencing it at the Bank of England's self-hosted version of Azure DevOps Server.

I previously couldn't produce a reprex, but I've now set up a publicly accessible project (`https://dev.azure.com/jameslairdsmith/Test`) on Azure DevOps Cloud for testing. title: Better sysreqs API
description:
1. [x] Print system packages needed for each package to be installed:

    ```
    > p$solve()
    > p$show_solution()

    + magrittr    2.0.3
    + pkgconfig   2.0.3
    + rlang       1.1.1
    ```
    This is not the best, because packages that are already installed might need system packages as well, and we actually try to install those as well. (Maybe we shouldn't?)
2. [x] Have a `sysreqs_platform` config option, to allow choosing the platform manually.
3. [x] Have functions to query the sysreqs DB and mappings. (See below.)
4. [x] ~~Have config option to install or just print sysreqs, when installing R packages.~~ Not needed, we can detect a good default, and you can already opt out.
5. [x] Auto-detect whether we can install sysreqs automatically, with or w/o sudo.
6. [x] Query installed system packages.
7. [x] Use this to print info about whether or not the required packages are installed.
8. [x] Use this to avoid trying to reinstall packages for every R package installation.
9. [x] Wrap functions from pak.
10. [x] Write a vignette/article in pak.
11. [x] Embed copy of sysreqs db into package.
12. [x] Do not fail if we cannot update sysreqs DB, but use cached or embedded deps, with a warning.
13. [x] Write individual sysreqs to the lock file, read it back from there.

As for the API, there are two pieces, one for package installations, and another one for independent queries. For package installations:
1. [x] `$show_sysreqs`
2. [x] `$get_sysreqs`: should info about whether it is already installed or not, maybe.
3. [x] `$install_sysreqs`

For independent queries:
1. [x] `sysreqs_platforms()`: list supported sysreqs platforms.
2. [x] `sysreqs_is_supported()`: check for sysreqs support on a platform.
1. [x] `sysreqs_db_list()`: list db contents for a platform.
3. [x] `sysreqs_db_match()`: match strings to the DB.
4. [x] `sysreqs_install_plan()`: make an install plan, get sysreqs.
5. [x] `sysreqs_check_installed()`: check that installed packages have their sysreqs installed.
6. [x] `sysreqs_list_system_packages()`: list installed system packages.

title: Handle package trees better
description:
Now creating a source R package is a separate step. This means:

* Download methods for the various remotes can produce either of these

  1. a proper source package
  2. a compressed (zip or tar.gz) file with a package tree
  3. an uncompressed package tree.

  A GH download will produce 2., a `local::` file will also produce 2., a `local::` directory will produce 3. 2. and 3. are produced at an alternate location (`target_tree`). We want to defer (un)compressing to installation time, that's why we support both 2. and 3.

* In the install plan, `file` will point to the tree, in case of 2. and 3.

* In the install plan, the new `packaged` column will denote whether `file` is a proper source package. 

* GitHub packages now do not do `R CMD build` upon downloading the package tree. This is good, because building might take a long time, or even fail, if the package needs to be installed because of dynamic manual pages, and some of its dependencies are missing.

* Local packages now copy the package file or directory into the download area, at download time.

Closes #131.

title: fix(resolve): try Archive/ on every configured repo for @version
description:
## Summary

`pkg@version` refs whose version is no longer in PACKAGES only looked in the Archive/ of the repo named `CRAN`. Now every repo in `options("repos")` is tried, in order:

```diff
 type_cran_resolve_version(remote)
   if version is in current PACKAGES
     return it
-  try <cran-mirror>/src/contrib/Archive/<pkg>/<pkg>_<ver>.tar.gz
-    RemoteRepos = cran-mirror
-  on error: resolve_from_metadata()
+  repos = unique(cran-mirror, options("repos"))
+  if repos is empty: resolve_from_metadata()
+  for repo in repos                      # CRAN mirror first
+    try <repo>/src/contrib/Archive/<pkg>/<pkg>_<ver>.tar.gz
+    on success: RemoteRepos = repo, stop
+  on error from all: resolve_from_metadata()
```

`type_cran_resolve_current()` (latest-version resolution) is unchanged.

## Evidence

New tests in `test-type-cran.R`, run with `NOT_CRAN=true` against `main`'s `R/type-cran.R` (before) and this branch (after):

```text
repos = c(CRAN = <primary, has pkg1 1.0.0>, archive = <has Archive/pkg1/pkg1_0.9.0.tar.gz>)
resolve("pkg1@0.9.0")
```

- **Before:** `status OK`, `version "1.0.0"`, `RemoteRepos` = CRAN url. The pinned ref silently resolves to the wrong version.
  **After:** `status OK`, `version "0.9.0"`, `RemoteRepos` = archive repo.
- **Before:** no repos configured: `Error in force(value): attempt to apply non-function`.
  **After:** falls back to `resolve_from_metadata()`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Resolution logic only. No stored state or migration; a revert restores the old behaviour.

**Blast Radius:** resolution

- Pinned refs (`pkg@ver`) can now resolve where they used to fail or resolve to the latest version. That's the fix, but lockfiles built with the old behaviour may differ.
- One extra HTTP request per additional repo, only when the CRAN mirror's Archive/ misses.

title: fix(resolve): try Archive/ on every configured repo for @version
description:
version-pinned refs used to only work for `cran` named repos

`type_cran_resolve_version()` previously only ever probed the CRAN mirror's
`src/contrib/Archive/<pkg>/<pkg>_<version>.tar.gz` path when resolving a
version-pinned ref (`pkg@version`) that isn't in the current PACKAGES index.
`config$get("cran-mirror")` resolves to `getOption("repos")["CRAN"]` specifically
- the one repo entry literally named "CRAN" - so any other configured
CRAN-like repo (e.g. an internal RDepot/Bioconductor-alike server that moves
superseded versions into its own Archive/ the same way CRAN does) was never
consulted, even though it follows the identical layout.

`type_cran_resolve_archive()` now tries the CRAN mirror's Archive first (same
as before, preserving the common case and avoiding extra network calls), then
recurses through every other repo in `options("repos")`, deduping by
trailing-slash-normalized URL. 
- Falls through to the existing resolve_from_metadata() catch-all if none of them have it. Only affects the version-pinned resolution path; 
- `type_cran_resolve_current()` (latest-version resolution) is untouched.

Collapses what was originally 3 helper functions (build URL list, resolve
list recursively, reverse-match winning URL back to a repo name) into 1
recursive helper that attaches `RemoteRepos` metadata directly from the repo
it just resolved against, instead of resolving output URL back to a source
